Some further information is given this week in mar correspondence column upon the "encroach Smut" question at Stockton Heath. Mr. Bouchier Tory fully and ebly stetes the case of the majority of the Parish Council who are in favour of what is spoken of .....compromise." The ratepayer', Should, therelore, be pretty well acquainted with I the pros and roux of the matter by the time the parish meet ng--at which, we understand, the Sul decision will be taken -is bell. There seetne,how- ever, will one or two points upon which some more light might be use( ully thrown. For instance, Mr. 'touchier states that the land was enclosed by the late Mr. Warburton under an arrangement with, or at the requeat of, the Highway Board. That la a tether important point, but it is a point which, one would think,rnigh, be readily settled one way or the Other. Transactions of that sort are recorded in the minutes of public authorities, and no doubt the minutes of the Highway Board of twenty-five years ago are still in existence and available for refer— ence. If the reulution of the Highway Board do- o. ducea Iniag 'st".renitere'nnttliecapnosiel, orof the majority of the Parish Council. Then, again, there is the statetnent,rnede last week that an offer was actuelly made to hand the lend over to the Pariah Council. If that offer was really made why was it not accepted? That is another point upon which same additional information might be given.,

A proposal to raise salaries can always he relied Woe to excite a discussion in the Warring-! ton Town Council, but the discussion '1 Upon the recommondation E. illefeCle Mr.' DIM salary from £350 to LI 0 0 was usually long and unummilly animated.No doubt this ins largely due to the fact that a lift of .CISO at one time of asking was a bit of a staggerer for some of the members. Something was sail during the debate upon the unpleasantness of these discussiona, but, after all, is the Comicil itself not to blame for this ? A Committee or sub-committee was ap- pointed some time ago to deal with the salaries officials and to settle them upon • permanent hams 801110.0.111 fies have been dealt with in that way,but others have not been considered. Until a uniform principle is applied all round these 'unpleasant " discussions are boned to crop up every now and again.

An important question wan raised by Councillor Plumpton though there was no discuseion upon it. Mr. Plumpton repreeente hitecrome ward and the pollution of Monkey Brook in an important matter for some of the remidents in Olt ward. The coun- cillor ham, therefore, made an excureion aloog the brook and he has discovered a thing or two that he did net know before. It would seem from bin! statement that the pollution of the Brook is not en- tinily due to the wicked chemical manufacturers o , Bt. Helene. Ile noticed& diecharge of liquid into the stream near Longford depot, from which an ex- tremely lively stench emanated, and he in now sceptical as to whether • nuisance is not created at the ford depot.
